mainTopic: רב ענן's view on the שחיטה of a משומד for עבודה זרה: proofs from יהושפט, אחאב and אליהו, and its refutation from ברייתות
overview: The גמרא is discussing רב ענן's view that a Jew who serves idols, like אחאב, can still do a kosher שחיטה. First it insists that יהושפט, a righteous king, did not keep himself apart from אחאב, and proves this from the two kings sitting facing each other like a סנהדרין. A support from אליהו, whom the ravens fed meat from אחאב's slaughterhouse, is pushed off because אליהו ate by the direct word of הקב"ה. A side discussion proves that those עורבים were real ravens. They were not two men named עורב, and not people from a place called עורב. Next, a ברייתא that lets "even a ישראל משומד" slaughter seems to support רב ענן. The גמרא explains that this משומד is someone who eats נבילות, following רבא. Finally, a ברייתא about who may bring קרבנות shows that a משומד for עבודה זרה counts as a משומד for the whole תורה, so רב ענן is fully refuted. The amud ends by asking whether the rule excluding a משומד from bringing קרבנות really comes from this פסוק or from a different one.

steps.title: יהושפט would not keep himself apart from אחאב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that יהושפט ate his own food separately from אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (יהושפט) would not have separated himself from him (אחאב).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier suggestion that יהושפט may have eaten his own food apart from אחאב. It says he would never have separated himself like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יהושפט ate separately, there is no proof that he relied on אחאב's שחיטה. By saying he never separated himself, the גמרא brings the proof back. Now the גמרא owes us a source for this claim.

phrases.english: He would not have separated himself from him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made just before this text that יהושפט ate on his own.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that יהושפט ate separately from אחאב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: יהושפט fully trusted אחאב and would not have kept himself apart.

steps.title: Where do we know this from? A first suggested verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source and suggests the פסוק "I am as you are, my people as your people."
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? If you say it is from the verse "I am as you are, my people as your people"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know יהושפט did not separate himself from אחאב. It offers a first possible source, and this sets up the next step, which will test that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion reads יהושפט's words "כמוני כמוך" as saying "I trust you as I trust myself." The word אילימא ("if you say") is a hint that this source will be knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?
if you say (a suggestion that usually gets rejected)

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
If you say it is from what is written:
"I am as you are, my people as your people,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the claim in step 1 and offers a first one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that יהושפט fully trusted אחאב.

steps.title: The same verse also says "my horses as your horses"
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails, because the same פסוק talks about horses, so it must mean "we share the same fate," not "we share the same trust."
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, does "my horses as your horses" also mean this? Rather, it means: what happens to your horses will happen to my horses. So too, what happens to you and your people will happen to me and my people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first proof. The same פסוק also says "my horses as your horses," and that cannot be about trust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Horses cannot be trusted or untrusted, so the whole פסוק must be about sharing a common fate in war. That means "I am as you are" tells us nothing about relying on אחאב's שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (introduces a problem with the reasoning)
is it the same here too?

phrases.english: But if so, "my horses as your horses": is it the same there too?
phrases.notes: These words come at the end of the same פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מָה דְּהָוֵי אַסּוּסֶיךָ תֶּהֱוֵי אַסּוּסַי,
phrases.english: Rather, it means: what will happen to your horses will happen to my horses,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי מַאי דְּהָוֵי עֲלָךְ וְעִילָּוֵי עַמָּךְ
phrases.english: so too, what will happen to you and to your people
will happen to me and to my people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using "כמוני כמוך" as a proof that יהושפט trusted אחאב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about sharing a fate in war, as "my horses as your horses" shows, not about trust.

steps.title: A better source: the two kings sitting at the gate of שומרון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new פסוק: the two kings sat on their thrones "in a threshing floor" at the gate of שומרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from here: "And the king of Israel and יהושפט king of Judah sat each on his throne, dressed in robes, in a threshing floor, at the entrance of the gate of שומרון."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new source for יהושפט's closeness with אחאב. It quotes the פסוק describing the two kings sitting together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on the strange word "בגורן" (in a threshing floor). The next steps explain this word and show how it proves the point.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, it is from here (a new source)
the gate of שומרון, אחאב's capital

phrases.english: Rather, it is from here:
"And the king of Israel and Yehoshafat king of Judah
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:10. The king of Israel here is אחאב.

phrases.english: were sitting, each on his throne,
dressed in robes,
in a threshing floor, at the entrance of the gate of Shomron."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source from steps 2-3 with a new one.
steps.raayaObject: That יהושפט was close with אחאב and relied on him.

steps.title: What does "threshing floor" mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what גורן means, since a city gate is not a real threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "threshing floor" mean? If you say an actual threshing floor, was the gate of שומרון a threshing floor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word גורן means in this פסוק. It rejects the simple meaning, and this sets up its own explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A city gate was where judges and elders met, not a place for threshing grain. So the word must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: is it really so that...? (shows something is unlikely)

phrases.english: What is "threshing floor"?
If you say an actual threshing floor,
was the gate of Shomron a threshing floor?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the key word in the פסוק brought in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of "גורן" in the פסוק.

steps.title: Sitting in a half-circle, like a סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: גורן means they sat in a curved shape like a threshing floor, the way a סנהדרין sat, so they could see each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means like a threshing floor, as we learned in a משנה: A סנהדרין was arranged like half of a round threshing floor, so that the judges could see each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the kings sat in a curved shape like a round threshing floor, facing each other. This finishes the proof that יהושפט was close with אחאב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סנהדרין sat in a half-circle so the judges could see one another and talk things through. The two kings sitting this way shows they discussed matters together as partners, so יהושפט relied on אחאב.

keyTerms.meaning: like half of a round threshing floor

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that יהושפט relied on אחאב is that they sat facing each other like a סנהדרין, not the words "כמוני כמוך."

phrases.english: Rather, it means like a threshing floor,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: סַנְהֶדְרִין הָיְתָה כַּחֲצִי גוֹרֶן עֲגוּלָּה
phrases.english: as we learned: A Sanhedrin was like half of a round threshing floor,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ רוֹאִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: so that they would see one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and completes the proof of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גורן means sitting in a round shape, facing each other, like a סנהדרין.

steps.title: A suggested support: the ravens brought אליהו meat from אחאב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אליהו eating meat from אחאב's slaughterhouse supports the view that אחאב's שחיטה was kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: "And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening." And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: from the slaughterhouse of אחאב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a possible support for the view that אחאב's שחיטה was valid. אליהו ate meat that came from אחאב's butchers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו was a great נביא and would not eat non-kosher meat. If he ate meat from אחאב's slaughterhouse, it seems אחאב's שחיטה was valid.

keyTerms.meaning: let us say this supports him

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב ענן, who holds that the שחיטה of a Jew who serves idols, like אחאב, is kosher.

phrases.english: "And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning,
and bread and meat in the evening,"
and Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
From the slaughterhouse of Achav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new possible support for the same view that אחאב's שחיטה was valid.
steps.raayaObject: רב ענן's view that the שחיטה of a משומד for עבודה זרה, like אחאב, is kosher.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 17:6 together with רב's teaching that the meat came from אחאב's slaughterhouse.

steps.title: אליהו ate by God's direct command
steps.stepSummary: The support is rejected: אליהו's case is different because he ate by the word of הקב"ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something done by the direct word of God is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from אליהו. Since הקב"ה told him to eat this food, his case teaches us nothing about normal הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When הקב"ה gives a special command, it can allow something that normally would not be allowed. So אליהו's eating does not prove that אחאב's שחיטה was kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: by the direct word of God

phrases.english: Something done by the word of God is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support offered in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from אליהו eating meat from אחאב's slaughterhouse.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אליהו acted on a special command from הקב"ה, which is not a normal halachic case.

steps.title: What were the עורבים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word עורבים in the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are "עורבים"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a side question about the same פסוק. It asks who or what the עורבים were, and this sets up the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עורבים usually means ravens, but it could also be a person's name. The next steps argue which meaning is correct.

phrases.english: What are "orevim"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether עורבים were birds or people.

steps.title: רבינא: real ravens
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the עורבים were actual ravens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: actual ravens.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers that the עורבים in the פסוק were real birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the plain meaning of the word. The next step challenges it.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Actual ravens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.

steps.title: Maybe they were two men named עורב
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מניומי suggests they might have been two men named עורב, since that was a real name in תנ"ך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מניומי said to him: Maybe they were two men whose names were עורב! Isn't it written: "And they killed עורב at the Rock of עורב, and זאב..."?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מניומי challenges רבינא. He points out that עורב was a real person's name, so maybe people brought אליהו the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is a פסוק in שופטים where a Midianite leader is named עורב. If עורב can be a name, the plain reading "ravens" is not the only possible one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Minyumi said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא תְּרֵי גַבְרֵי דְּהָוֵי שְׁמַיְיהוּ עוֹרְבִים!
phrases.english: But perhaps they were two men whose names were Orev!
Isn't it written:
"And they killed Orev at the Rock of Orev,
and Ze'ev, etc."?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי: וְדִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that עורבים were actual ravens.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עורב is a known person's name in שופטים, so the word could mean people named עורב.

steps.title: Both just happened to be named עורב?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that it is very unlikely both men happened to have the same name, so they must have been real ravens.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did it just happen that both of them were named עורב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends his view. It would be too much of a coincidence for both people bringing the food to be named עורב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the word is plural, there had to be at least two of them. Two people with the same unusual name is very unlikely, so the plain meaning, real ravens, wins.
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא holds that the עורבים who fed אליהו were real ravens, because two men both named עורב would be too unlikely a coincidence.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did the matter just happen by chance
that both of them were named Orev?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבינא answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עורבים might be two men named עורב.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is too unlikely that both were named עורב, so they were real ravens.

steps.title: Maybe the עורבים were named after their hometown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the עורבים were people named after a place called עורב. It brings a similar case where רבי פדת explained נערה as a place name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe they were called עורבים after the place they came from! Isn't it written: 'And Aram went out in bands and captured from the land of Israel a young girl, a minor'? We found it hard that the פסוק calls her both 'young woman' and 'minor.' רבי פדת explained: she was a minor girl from a place called נעורן!
steps.whatsHappening: After רבינא proved the עורבים were not two men with the same name, the גמרא raises a new possibility. Maybe they were two men from a place called עורב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's argument was that two men are unlikely to share one personal name. A shared hometown name avoids that problem, because many people come from the same town. The case of the נערה shows that a פסוק can call a person by a word that is really a place name.

keyTerms.meaning: Named after their place of origin
A young woman (an older stage than a minor)

phrases.english: And perhaps they were named after their place!
Is it not written:
"And Aram went out in bands
and took captive from the land of Israel a young minor girl"
and it was difficult for us:
it calls her a "young woman" and also calls her a "minor"
phrases.notes: These are two different ages, so a girl can't be both at once.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Pedat said:
a minor who was from Naaran!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around רבינא's answer in step 12 by offering a shared place name in place of a shared personal name.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the עורבים were real ravens
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two men could easily share a hometown name. The case of the נערה from נעורן shows that a פסוק can describe people by their place.

steps.title: The פסוק would have said עורביים
steps.stepSummary: If they came from a place called עורב, the פסוק would have used the form עורביים, meaning 'Orebites.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said 'עורביים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the hometown idea by looking at the exact form of the word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People named after a place are called by a form with the ending '-י' (for example, Orebites). The פסוק says עורבים and not עורביים, so it is not describing a hometown. That leaves רבינא's reading: real ravens.

keyTerms.meaning: Orebites: people from a place called עורב

steps.whatToRemember: The עורבים who fed אליהו were real ravens. They were not men named עורב and not people from a place called עורב.

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said "Orebites".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hometown suggestion of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עורבים might be men from a place called עורב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word would then have the place-name form עורביים. Since it says עורבים, they were real ravens.

steps.title: A ברייתא that may support רב ענן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying everyone may slaughter, even a כותי, a ערל, and a ישראל משומד. It suggests this supports רב ענן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: Everyone may slaughter, even a כותי, even a ערל, and even a ישראל משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב ענן's view about a משומד's שחיטה. It brings a ברייתא that might back him up, and is setting up an analysis of this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly allows a ישראל משומד to slaughter. If that משומד can be shown to be a משומד for עבודה זרה, רב ענן is supported. The next steps try to prove exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say that this supports him
A Jew who regularly breaks a מצוה on purpose

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב ענן, whose view about a משומד the גמרא discussed earlier.

phrases.english: Everyone may slaughter, and even a Samaritan,
and even an uncircumcised man,
and even a Jewish transgressor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the עורבים ends, the גמרא brings a new proof for רב ענן, since the proof from אליהו was rejected in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב ענן's view that one may eat from the שחיטה of a משומד for עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: הכל שוחטין, ואפילו כותי, ואפילו ערל, ואפילו ישראל משומד

steps.title: Who is the ערל in the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of ערל the ברייתא means. It rejects a ערל whose brothers died from מילה, because he is a fully proper Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ערל, what is the case? If you say it is one whose brothers died because of מילה, he is a fully proper Jew!
steps.whatsHappening: To build the proof, the גמרא first pins down who the ערל in the ברייתא is. It tests one possibility and rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man whose brothers died from מילה is allowed to stay uncircumcised, so he has done nothing wrong. There would be no reason to say 'even' about him. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
His brothers died because of circumcision

phrases.english: This uncircumcised man, what is the case?
If you say it is one whose brothers died because of circumcision,
this one is a fully proper Jew!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins analyzing the ברייתא from step 15 to build the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of ערל the ברייתא is talking about

steps.title: The ערל is a משומד for not doing מילה
steps.stepSummary: The ערל must be someone who stays uncircumcised on purpose, a משומד לערלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he is a משומד for staying uncircumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ערל in the ברייתא is a man who refuses מילה on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the innocent ערל was ruled out, the ערל must be a sinner. His sin is one specific מצוה‎, מילה. This detail is the base for the argument about the סיפא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A transgressor who refuses circumcision on purpose

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that he is a transgressor regarding staying uncircumcised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ערל is a משומד לערלות: one who refuses מילה on purpose.

steps.title: So the later משומד must be for עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's ישראל משומד cannot be a sinner in one matter, since that is just like the ערל. So it must be a משומד for עבודה זרה, which matches רב ענן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last part: 'and even a ישראל משומד.' What is the case? If he is a משומד for one matter, that is the same as the משומד for staying uncircumcised. Rather, isn't it a משומד for עבודה זרה, which matches רב ענן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It shows the last case in the ברייתא must be a משומד for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would not list the same case twice. The ערל already covers a person who sins in one matter, so the 'ישראל משומד' must be something new and worse: a משומד for עבודה זרה. Since the ברייתא allows him to slaughter, it supports רב ענן.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the last part (of the ברייתא)
A transgressor in one specific matter

phrases.english: Say the last part:
"and even a Jewish transgressor": what is the case?
If he is a transgressor in one matter,
that is the same as the transgressor regarding staying uncircumcised,
rather, is it not a transgressor regarding idol worship,
and this matches Rav Anan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 17 (the ערל is a משומד in one matter) to identify the משומד in the סיפא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's סיפא, read as a משומד for עבודה זרה because a משומד in one matter is already covered by the ערל

steps.title: A משומד for עבודה זרה cannot slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. A משומד for עבודה זרה is not allowed to slaughter, because עבודה זרה is so severe that denying it is like accepting the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really I will tell you: a משומד for עבודה זרה may not slaughter. As the Master said: עבודה זרה is severe, since anyone who denies it is like someone who accepts the entire תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב ענן. It says the ברייתא cannot be talking about a משומד for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Denying עבודה זרה counts as accepting the whole תורה. So someone who serves idols is like someone who rejects the whole תורה, and his שחיטה is not valid. This means the ברייתא's משומד must be some other case, and the גמרא still has to explain how it differs from the ערל.

keyTerms.meaning: Really I will tell you (introduces a rejection)
עבודה זרה is a severe sin
Like one who accepts the whole תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the ברייתא's last case means nothing. It only says that case cannot be a משומד for עבודה זרה. The ברייתא still needs some other explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a משומד for עבודה זרה is treated like someone who rejects the whole תורה, and his שחיטה is not valid.

phrases.english: No, really I will say to you:
a transgressor regarding idol worship may not slaughter,
as the Master said:
Idol worship is severe,
since anyone who denies it
is like one who accepts the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רב ענן built in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא's ישראל משומד as a משומד for עבודה זרה, which takes away the support for רב ענן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משומד for עבודה זרה counts as rejecting the entire תורה, so a ברייתא could not allow his שחיטה.

steps.title: The ברייתא's ישראל משומד is a sinner in eating נבילות
steps.stepSummary: The ישראל משומד who may slaughter in the ברייתא is a משומד in the same matter, eating נבילות, and this fits רבא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ישראל משומד in the ברייתא is someone who sins in that very matter, and this follows רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא's ישראל משומד can't be a משומד for עבודה זרה, so the גמרא now says who he really is. He is someone who eats non-kosher meat (נבילות), the very sin connected to slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 claimed the ישראל משומד can't be a 'one-matter' sinner, because that would make him the same as the ערל. The answer is that he is a different case: the ערל sins in another matter, but this man sins in the same matter as slaughtering. רבא already ruled that such a person (one who eats נבילות because they are easier) may slaughter if we check his knife first, so the ברייתא is not a proof for רב ענן.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner in that very same matter, here eating meat that was not properly slaughtered
An animal that died without a kosher slaughter; forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for רב ענן is gone. The ברייתא's ישראל משומד is one who eats נבילות, and רבא already allows him to slaughter if we check his knife.

phrases.english: Rather, it means a sinner regarding that same matter,
phrases.notes: 'That same matter' means eating meat that wasn't properly slaughtered, the sin that touches on slaughtering.

phrases.english: and it is like רבא's ruling.
phrases.notes: רבא said earlier that we check such a person's knife, and then he may slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection in step 19 by giving a new meaning for the ברייתא's ישראל משומד
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If the ישראל משומד is not a משומד for עבודה זרה, who is he?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A משומד for eating נבילות, who may slaughter according to רבא

steps.title: A ברייתא about which Jews may bring קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that excludes a משומד from bringing קרבנות, while allowing ordinary Jewish sinners, and sets it up as a challenge to רב ענן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'From you' means not all of you, so a משומד is left out. 'From you' also means I made this split only among you, not among the nations. 'From the animal' includes people who act like animals. From here they said: we accept קרבנות from Jewish sinners so they will come back in תשובה, except for a משומד, one who pours wine for idols, and one who breaks שבת in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge to רב ענן by quoting a ברייתא about who may bring a קרבן. The full challenge comes later, so this step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that some Jews can't bring קרבנות, but non-Jews always can. It accepts קרבנות from Jewish sinners to help them do תשובה, and it lists exceptions: a משומד, one who pours wine for idols, and one who breaks שבת in public. Before the גמרא can use this against רב ענן, it first has to deal with a problem inside the ברייתא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought in the בית המקדש
One who pours wine as an offering to an idol

phrases.english: They challenged: 'From you' and not all of you,
to leave out the משומד.
'From you': among you I made a split,
and not among the nations.
'From the animal': to include
people who are like animals.
From here they said: we accept offerings
from Jewish sinners
so that they will come back in repentance through them,
except for the משומד,
and one who pours wine to idols,
and one who breaks שבת in public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רב ענן after the earlier proof was rejected
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ענן's view about a משומד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's list of who is excluded from bringing קרבנות will be used against רב ענן; the full attack comes after the ברייתא is first explained

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the ברייתא excludes a משומד from bringing קרבנות, but the next part accepts קרבנות from Jewish sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is hard. You said 'From you, and not all of you' leaves out the משומד, and then it teaches that we accept קרבנות from Jewish sinners!
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא, the גמרא points out that its parts seem to clash with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משומד is a kind of sinner. So how can the ברייתא first say a משומד's קרבן is turned away, and then say sinners' קרבנות are accepted? The גמרא has to sort out the ברייתא before it can use it.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult; it seems to contradict itself
And then it goes on to teach

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
you said: 'From you' and not all of you,
to leave out the משומד,
and then it teaches:
we accept offerings from Jewish sinners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out an internal contradiction in the ברייתא just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא itself (first part against middle part)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משומד is a sinner, so excluding him clashes with accepting קרבנות from sinners

steps.title: Whole-תורה sinner versus one-matter sinner
steps.stepSummary: The first part speaks about a משומד for the entire תורה. The middle part speaks about a משומד for one matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not hard. The first part means a משומד for the whole תורה. The middle part means a משומד for one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying each part of the ברייתא is talking about a different kind of sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who rejects the whole תורה can't bring a קרבן. Someone who sins in only one area can bring one, so that it helps him come back. Now the ברייתא makes sense, and the גמרא can go on to use it in its challenge to רב ענן.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a source
The middle part of a source
A sinner who rejects the entire תורה
A sinner in only one area

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא has three parts: the first part ('not all of you'), the middle part ('we accept from sinners'), and the end ('except for the משומד...'). Here the גמרא is only matching the first and middle parts.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
the first part means a משומד for the entire תורה,
the middle part means a משומד for one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, רֵישָׁא – מְשׁוּמָּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each clause is about a different type of sinner
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses seemed to be about the same kind of sinner, so they clashed
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is about a sinner against the whole תורה, and the middle clause is about a sinner in one matter

steps.title: Who is the מְשׁוּמָּד in the last part of the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The last part of the ברייתא excludes a מְשׁוּמָּד. Either kind of מְשׁוּמָּד creates a problem: it repeats the first part or contradicts the middle part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the last part: 'except for the מְשׁוּמָּד, and one who pours wine to idols, and one who breaks שבת in public.' What kind of מְשׁוּמָּד is this? If he rejects the whole תורה, that was already taught in the first part. If he rejects only one matter, that contradicts the middle part, which accepts קרבנות from such a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last part of the ברייתא. It shows that the word 'מְשׁוּמָּד' there can't mean either type it has just defined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, the first part was about a מְשׁוּמָּד for the whole תורה, and the middle part was about a מְשׁוּמָּד for one matter. If the סיפא is also about a whole-תורה מְשׁוּמָּד, it is extra and teaches nothing. If it is about a one-matter מְשׁוּמָּד, it says the opposite of the middle part, so both options fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
What is the case? What exactly does this mean?
Pours wine as an offering to an idol

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
Except for the transgressor,
and one who pours wine as an offering
phrases.notes: He means pouring wine as an offering to an idol.

phrases.english: and one who desecrates Shabbat in public.
This transgressor, what is the case?
If he is a transgressor for the entire Torah,
that is the same as the first clause,
and if he is a transgressor for one matter,
the middle clause is difficult.
phrases.notes: The middle part, from step 23, accepts קרבנות from someone who sins in just one matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definitions from step 23 to examine the last part of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of 'מְשׁוּמָּד' in the סיפא of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either reading fails. A whole-תורה מְשׁוּמָּד repeats the רישא, and a one-matter מְשׁוּמָּד contradicts the מציעתא.

steps.title: Reading the last part as describing one kind of מְשׁוּמָּד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the סיפא as one category: a מְשׁוּמָּד to pour wine to idols or to break שבת in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא must mean this: 'except for the one who is a מְשׁוּמָּד to pour wine to idols and to break שבת in public.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by reading the סיפא differently. It is not a list of three separate people. It describes one kind of מְשׁוּמָּד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'the מְשׁוּמָּד, AND one who pours wine, AND one who breaks שבת,' the גמרא reads 'the מְשׁוּמָּד TO pour wine and TO break שבת.' Now the סיפא is neither extra nor contradictory. It adds a new rule: these specific sins put a person in the most serious group.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't this what it means? (introduces a new reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the סיפא as a list of three different people. The גמרא changes 'וּמְנַסֵּךְ' (and one who pours) to 'לְנַסֵּךְ' (to pour). The words now describe what kind of מְשׁוּמָּד he is.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִן הַמְשׁוּמָּד לְנַסֵּךְ אֶת הַיַּיִן
phrases.english: Except for the transgressor who pours wine to idols
or desecrates Shabbatot in public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from step 24 by rereading the סיפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא lists three separate excluded people, which made it either repeat the רישא or contradict the מציעתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא describes one category: a מְשׁוּמָּד for idolatrous wine-pouring or public שבת desecration

steps.title: עבודה זרה counts as the whole תורה: a refutation of רב ענן
steps.stepSummary: The new reading shows that a מְשׁוּמָּד for עבודה זרה is treated as a מְשׁוּמָּד for the whole תורה, so רב ענן is fully refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that a מְשׁוּמָּד for עבודה זרה counts as a מְשׁוּמָּד for the whole תורה. This is a refutation of רב ענן, and it is indeed a full refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the new reading and says that רב ענן's view cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא excludes this מְשׁוּמָּד from bringing קרבנות, just like the whole-תורה מְשׁוּמָּד of the רישא. So the ברייתא treats עבודה זרה (and public שבת desecration) like rejecting the whole תורה. That goes against רב ענן, who did not treat a מְשׁוּמָּד for עבודה זרה as a מְשׁוּמָּד for the whole תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who has turned away to idol worship
A refutation; when repeated, it means the refutation is final

steps.whatToRemember: A מְשׁוּמָּד for עבודה זרה or for public חילול שבת is treated like a מְשׁוּמָּד for the entire תורה. רב ענן's opposing view is refuted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic status of an idol-worshipper or public שבת desecrator: he is treated like someone who has rejected the whole תורה.

phrases.english: Apparently, a transgressor for idol worship
is a transgressor for the entire Torah,
and this is a refutation of Rav Anan.
It is a conclusive refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא מְשׁוּמָּד לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הָוֵה מְשׁוּמָּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic lesson from the reading in step 25 and completes the challenge to רב ענן begun in step 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מְשׁוּמָּד for עבודה זרה is a מְשׁוּמָּד for the whole תורה, and רב ענן is conclusively refuted

steps.title: Is the rule really learned from this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the source: the rule that we don't accept קרבנות from a מְשׁוּמָּד seems to come from a different פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this rule really learned from here? It is learned from there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about where the rule comes from. This line sets up the next move, and the other פסוק will be quoted right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned from the words 'מִכֶּם' (of you, not all of you) that a מְשׁוּמָּד is excluded. The גמרא now points out that this exclusion is already taught by a different פסוק, about a חטאת. So why would the ברייתא need this פסוק?

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from there (from another source)

phrases.english: But is this derived from here?
It is derived from there,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation is settled, the גמרא turns to question the ברייתא's source for excluding a מְשׁוּמָּד
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'מִכֶּם' to exclude a מְשׁוּמָּד from bringing קרבנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion already comes from a different פסוק about a חטאת, so learning it here seems unnecessary
